questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Although the ECB backed Brendon McCullum in March 2026 after the 4-1 Ashes defeat, England have lost six of their last eight Tests and face intense scrutiny after the Stokes/Atkinson curfew breach and 253-run Oval loss to New Zealand ahead of the June 25 decider. If the ECB replaces McCullum or splits Test/white-ball roles before the August Pakistan series, recently available ex-Afghanistan coach Jonathan Trott (52 Tests for England, publicly eager for the role) and ECB-contracted England Lions coach Andrew Flintoff (backed by Rob Key) are the two most prominently linked candidates. Former Ashes-winning coach Andy Flower, internal England batting assistant Marcus Trescothick, and Rajasthan Royals director Kumar Sangakkara round out the top five, with substantial 45% field uncertainty covering Gary Kirsten, Ravi Shastri, Justin Langer, Alec Stewart, and surprise ECB hires.
